tei:div.tei:p: A psalm, a song for the dedication of the house; by David.

I extol thee, O Lord, for thou hast lifted me, and hast not let my foes rejoice over me. Lord my God, I cried to thee, and thou didst heal me. O Lord, thou hast lifted me up from the grave; thou hast let me live, that I should not go down to the pit. Sing to the Lord, you who are godly, and give thanks to his holy name. For his anger only lasts a moment, but his favor lasts a lifetime; weeping may lodge with us at evening, but in the morning there are shouts of joy. I thought in my security I never would be shaken. O Lord, by thy favor thou hadst established my mountain as a stronghold; but when thy favor was withdrawn, I was dismayed. To thee, O Lord, I called; I appealed to my God: “What profit would my blood be, if I went down to the grave? Will the dust praise thee? Will it declare thy faithfulness? Hear, O Lord, and be gracious to me; Lord, be thou my helper.” Thou hast changed my mourning into dancing; thou hast put off my sackcloth and girded me with joy;
so that my soul may praise thee, and not be silent. Lord my God, I will thank thee forever.
